![Sofia Emelianova](https://web.dev/images/authors/sofiayem.jpg) Sofia Emelianova [GitHub](https://github.com/sofiayem)

<br />

This guide shows you how to use [Chrome DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools) to do the following:

- Test if you optimized your page for instant loads when using the browser's back and forward buttons.
- Identify issues that may prevent your page from being eligible for this type of caching.

[Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y2IVv5KnrmI)

Back/forward cache (or bfcache) is a browser optimization that enables instant back and forward navigation. For more information, see [Back/forward cache](https://web.dev/articles/bfcache).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key point:** Back/forward cache differs from browser [cache](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Cache) and [HTTP cache](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Caching).   
>
> To inspect [cache](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Cache) data, follow the steps in [View cache data](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/storage/cache).   
>
> To inspect [HTTP cache](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Caching) data, open the **Size** column of the **Network Log** . See [Log network activity](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/network#load).

## Test back/forward cache

To test back/forward cache, follow these steps:

1. On your page, [open DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/open), then navigate to **Application** \> **Background services** \> **Back/forward cache**.

   ![Back/forward cache tab.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/backforward-cache-tab-a5b7dab553d61.png)
2. Click **Test back/forward cache**.

   Chrome automatically takes you to `chrome://terms/` and back to your page.

   Alternatively, you can click the browser's back and forward buttons.

If the back/forward cache works for your page with no issues, you'll see the following message:

![Successfully served from back/forward cache.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/successfully-served-back-9dc3e53733a32.png)

Otherwise, you'll see a list of issues.

To find out which issues affect which frames, expand the **Frames** ![Expand icon.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/expand-icon-0dbf0d5585cf5.svg) section.

![Expanded Frames section.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/expanded-frames-section-3bad0294b3223.png)

## Resolve issues that prevent caching

If your page isn't eligible for back/forward caching, the **Back/forward cache** tab shows you a list with three types of causes:

![Not eligible for back/forward cache.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/not-eligible-backforwar-ce70c84e43e74.png)

- **Actionable** . You can fix these issues to enable caching. For example, [stop using `unload` events](https://web.dev/articles/bfcache#never_use_the_unload_event).
- **Pending Support**. Chrome doesn't support these features yet, so they prevent caching. However, once supported, Chrome removes these limitations.
- **Not Actionable**. You can't fix these issues on this page. Something that is outside the page's control prevents caching.

To find out which frame is the blocker, expand the corresponding section under the issue's description.

![Blocking frames.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/application/back-forward-cache/image/blocking-frames-82bd55fd07fac.png)

## Common issues that prevent back/forward caching

The two main reasons that prevent bfcache from running are:

- [`Cache-Control: no-store` header](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Cache-Control).

  This header value is recommended for pages with personal and private information. For pages you want to be reasonably fresh, use `no-cache` or a short cache time, for example, `max-age=60`.
- [Problematic unload handlers](https://web.dev/articles/bfcache#never_use_the_unload_event).

  Chrome is planning to [deprecate unload handlers](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/deprecating-unload) and recommends to never use an `unload` event.

  To ensure that your website doesn't use unload handlers and, for example, prevent extensions from adding `unload` events, declare the `Permissions-Policy: unload=()` HTTP response header.

> [!TIP]
> **Tip:** To test a bfcache fix, you can [mock a response header with overrides](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/overrides).
